text:
alex_m: Heads-up — customer report (ticket #12345) of intermittent 502s from hosted embeddings in eu1 around 10:23 UTC. They see `upstream prematurely closed connection` and early stream resets.

maya_k: Copy. Can you paste a minimal repro / trace-id?

alex_m: Customer sent this curl (http2):
```
curl -v --http2 -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" -d '{"input":"hello"}' https://eu1.api.redwood.com/v1/embeddings
```
Trace IDs: 01FZB2... / 01FZB9... attached in ticket.

john_s: I pulled ingress-nginx logs for the window. Frequent lines: `upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream`, plus `http2: stream canceled` and a handful of `window update` warnings. Repro I ran:
```
for i in {1..100}; do curl --http2 -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"input":"x"}' https://eu1.api.redwood.com/v1/embeddings & done; wait
```
After ~30s I see 502s from the frontdoor and nginx emits `SEND_RST_STREAM` to upstreams.

emily_r: Observed on infra side: upstream pods (model-serving) do not show CPU or OOM spikes. Latency is low for successful streams. Error pattern fits an http2 pipeline stall where many small concurrent streams + backend chunked responses cause proxy buffers to backpressure and nginx resets streams. Config notes: we use `proxy_http_version 1.1` in a handful of routes, but embeddings frontdoor is still h2.

maya_k: Quick mitigation options: 1) Ask customer to reduce client concurrency or add short jitter, 2) flip that frontdoor to http/1.1 to avoid h2 multiplexing, 3) route heavy embed traffic to a dedicated pool. Which do we want to try first?

alex_m: I pushed a canary to force http1 on one eu1 frontdoor host (canary id: canary/ingress-eu1-ht1) — patch: https://phabricator/redwood/CL/33421. Monitoring: 10m post-change saw 90% reduction in 502s for that host.

john_s: I created ENG-4321 and attached nginx debug + tcpdump + repro script. Marked eng-runtime and eng-sre. Notes in ticket: probable nginx http2 flow-control bug combined with `proxy_buffering` interactions and upstream keepalive reuse.

sre-bot: deploy-bot: canary apply succeeded (ingress-eu1-ht1) at 11:05 UTC.

emily_r: Customer updated with workaround (reduce concurrency / use retry with backoff) and we offered temporary routing to dedicated capacity. Customer accepted the http1 canary as immediate mitigation. ETA for full fix: 24-48h pending eng-runtime triage.

maya_k: For postmortem / follow-ups: capture full pcap + nginx debug on failure window, add an e2e test that drives many small http2 streaming embed requests, and consider switching default frontdoor to http1 for embeddings until kernel/h2 fixes land.

alex_m: Thanks all — saving logs in ticket and ENG-4321. Assigning follow-ups: eng-runtime (owner), eng-sre (monitoring), support (customer comms). :thumbsup:
